newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dlr seen extending gains vs mark, yen in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Dlr seen extending gains vs mark, yen in Singapore.

text.p: The dollar looked set to head for 119 yen after its overnight spike up but profit-taking interest from short-term players was likely to slow its rise, and after a pause it was seen resuming its uptrend on the mark, Singapore-based dealers said on Wednesday.
The dollar was boosted by Japan's industrial output data, showing a 3.1 percent month-on-month fall in June, against an average forecast of a 2.8 percent fall.
Dealers said the dollar's uptrend remained intact and it was likely to target the 120 yen level within a week.

"Japanese exporters are hedged quite substantially already at the lower levels. Of course we will see continuous hedging but the market always tries to buy the dollar on dips and locks in profits on any moves up," a European bank dealer said.
The dollar was taking a breather against the mark but it had remained well supported around 1.8250 marks and was likely to head higher after some consolidation, dealers said.
"The dollar's poised to retest 1.85 marks again and in the longer term, it should go up to 1.92," the dealer said.
He said players might start bailing out above the 1.92 mark level but the extent of the dollar's rally would depend largely on external factors and political comments out of Europe.
Sterling/mark, which appeared to have topped out at its recent highs above 3.0 marks, would also be a key factor.
The dealer said there was a growing perception that Britain would not hike rates much further whereas the Bundesbank was expected to start raising German rates sooner rather than later.
"We believe (German rates) will be stable near three percent for now. Maybe the Bundesbank will keep the fantasy open but we won't see any rate hike in the next two to four weeks," he added.
